classification.difficultyReason: Translate three different sets of colour choices into tree stages and identify paths with all three colours distinct despite restrictions at each stage.

content.prompt: A painter is going to paint a child’s bedroom. He has two choices of colour for the ceiling, blue or white; he has three choices of colour for the walls, blue, grey or white; and he has two choices of colour for the skirting boards, grey or white. He has to choose the colour for the ceiling, the walls and the skirting boards.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a tree diagram showing all the outcomes.

answer.short: Use $B=$ blue, $G=$ grey and $W=$ white. In ceiling–walls–skirting order, the outcomes are $BBG, BBW, BGG, BGW, BWG, BWW, WBG, WBW, WGG, WGW, WWG, WWW$.
answer.worked: The stages are ceiling, walls and skirting boards. Branch first into $B,W$, then into $B,G,W$ from each ceiling choice, and finally into $G,W$ from each wall choice. There are $2\times3\times2=12$ outcomes.

spec.description: Three-stage tree with 2 ceiling branches, 3 wall branches per ceiling and 2 skirting branches per wall. Colour names are represented by editable letter labels, with no decorative colour.
spec.mathematics: Twelve ordered outcomes with stage choice sets {B,W}, {B,G,W}, {G,W}.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If he chooses at random, what is the probability that the ceiling, the walls and the skirting boards are painted different colours?

answer.worked:
In ceiling–walls–skirting order, the favourable outcomes are $BGW, BWG, WBG$. There are 3 favourable paths among 12 equally likely paths.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{all different colours})&=\frac3{12}\\P(\text{all different colours})&=\frac14\end{align*}$$
